The task#

Question. Are hand hygiene interventions effective in reducing healthcare-associated infections?

The topic is deliberately obvious and uncontroversial, so that your attention goes to the method: how an AI tool screens abstracts and extracts data, where it fails, and how you would notice. You will compare what the AI does with the reference review: Pruna et al., J Clin Med 2026, a systematic review of quasi-experimental studies in acute care hospitals with 12 included studies, in which two independent human reviewers did the screening, extraction, risk of bias and synthesis without generative AI (the authors declare Rayyan for duplicate detection and the screening workflow, and ChatGPT for English-language editing only). Its decisions are the answers you compare with. The choice was confirmed by the workshop team on 6 November 2026; citation, reasons and limits are in data/README.md. Open the review after the exercise, not before: it names the included studies.

What you do: you screen 20 records and extract 5 fields from one paper with any generative AI, then compare with the human reviewers.

This page is the guide for the live session (EPH 2026, Bilbao) and for anyone doing the exercise alone, months later, without a facilitator or the slides: if that is you, start with Doing it on your own (self-paced).

The point of the exercise. AI can bring real advantages to evidence synthesis (speed, scale, consistency, living updates), but only in the hands of people with AI literacy and advanced skills. Without understanding how these systems work you can make serious errors without seeing them, and lose control of the process. The human reviewer stays responsible for every decision. These skills are necessary, not sufficient: they work together with review methods expertise and a verification workflow. In this exercise you practise the checks that keep you in the loop.
Time Live session: 30 minutes on your own, inside a 60-minute session. On your own, later: 60 to 90 minutes (self-paced path)
You need a phone or a laptop and any generative AI: a chat app (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Mistral...) on Route 1, or a coding agent on Route 2
How individually: each person on their own phone or laptop. You drive the AI, then you verify it
Three moves 1 screen 20 records and paste the AI's answer into the scorer · 2 look at two of its errors · 3 extract 5 fields from one paper, with quotes
Not finishing is expected. Two errors you understand are worth more than twenty decisions you did not check

The demo#

Before you start, watch the demo video (about 2 minutes, silent, with captions): one repository, your AI, your way. The repository holds the materials; the video shows two ways to bring them to an AI (Route 1, copy and paste on a phone; Route 2, connect an AI agent to a clone of the repository on a laptop) and then the same checks whatever the route: the scorer, and one quote found in the paper. The AI answers in it are real, recorded on 6 November 2026 (a chat assistant with the prompts of this site, and an AI coding agent on a fresh clone, web search off) and shown unedited. It uses batch 3 (R041-R060) and the paper Mestre2012, so that nothing you will work on is shown in advance: you do the same on batch 1 and Phan2020, in the way you prefer. In the room, Francesco Baglivo comments it live and Patrick Boudreau speaks for the verifier. Today, on your own, you do both: you drive the AI, then you verify it (see Working on your own).

On GitHub: the video (MP4), its captions (WebVTT), and what it shows, with the raw AI answers.

Not at the session? Watch the video above: it shows the three steps without a facilitator. The talks are not needed to do the exercise: the key message is above, and the self-paced path below replaces the facilitators and the slides.

Working on your own#

Everyone works individually, on their own laptop: you drive the AI, then you verify it. First you paste the prompt and the records and let the AI answer; then you stop and check what it said against the source, the abstract or the paper, before you believe it. A laptop is recommended (copying, pasting and reading two windows side by side); a phone works for reading the pages and the answers. If you like, compare your errors with your neighbour's after step 2 (optional). In the discussion each person brings one error they found.

For learning only. These prompts are teaching material for this workshop. They are not a validated method. If you are not confident with how large language models work (context windows, parsing, sampling, retrieval, hallucination) and with advanced techniques (structured outputs, verification against the source, reproducibility checks, documentation of model and version), do not use AI to conduct a real evidence review. You stay responsible for every decision: the AI does not.

Three rules for both tracks.

  1. Turn off web search / browsing and use a temporary chat (memory off). In the previous run of this workshop (Berlin, September 2026) a chat assistant with internet access recognised the published reference review and offered to repeat it. The reference review here (Pruna et al. 2026) is published too: an AI with web access may simply look up the answers. Agent track: do not allow web search or web fetch tools.

  2. Screening answers after step 1, extraction answers after step 3: do not open the reference answers earlier.

  3. Upload or paste only texts whose licence allows it (the license column of the records, the licence column of data/papers.csv), and never personal or confidential data.

The eligibility criteria (from the reference review)#

PICO: P patients and healthcare workers in acute care hospitals · I hospital-wide or multi-ward multimodal hand hygiene intervention · C pre-intervention period, standard practice or a contemporaneous comparator · O clinical healthcare-associated infection outcomes · Design quasi-experimental studies.

A record is included only if it meets all of C1 to C6. Paste these criteria into your prompt word for word (they are also in review_config.yaml, which contains no answers).

Criterion Include Exclude
C1 Setting Acute care hospital (general, tertiary referral or teaching hospital providing short-term inpatient care) Only long-term care, nursing homes, outpatient or ambulatory care, rehabilitation; veterinary settings
C2 Scope Implemented hospital-wide or across more than one inpatient ward or department Only a single ICU, neonatal ICU, emergency department or any other isolated single unit
C3 Intervention Multimodal hand hygiene intervention (at least two components, e.g. education, reminders, audit and feedback, hand rub availability, leadership, champions) that is the clearly central focus A single isolated measure (posters alone, glove policy, product comparison, electronic monitoring alone); broad infection-prevention bundles (screening, isolation, cohorting, cleaning, stewardship) where hand hygiene is one component whose contribution cannot be interpreted
C4 Design Interrupted time series, controlled before-after, or uncontrolled before-after with clearly defined pre- and post-intervention periods Randomised trials (including cluster), cross-sectional or descriptive studies, outbreak reports, case reports, editorials, letters, conference abstracts, reviews
C5 Outcome At least one clinical HAI outcome (overall HAI rate, CLABSI, CAUTI, VAP, C. difficile infection, MRSA or VRE acquisition or infection, other defined hospital-acquired infection) Only process measures (compliance, hand rub consumption, knowledge, microbial counts on hands)
C6 Language English (no date limits) Other languages

At title/abstract stage, if the abstract does not let you decide, the answer is unsure, not exclude.

Step 1 · Screening (10 min)#

  1. Route 1: one tap. On the Start page tap Copy prompt + 20 records: you get the screening prompt (the criteria C1-C6 are already in) with the 20 records of batch 1 (R001-R020) inserted where it says [PASTE THE RECORDS HERE]. Paste it into a new temporary chat, web search off, and go to point 4. Route 2: ask your agent in plain words (see the table above). To copy the pieces separately instead, continue with points 2 and 3. Copy the records: open the records page and copy batch 1 (R001-R020) with one tap. Some abstracts are empty in the repository because their licence does not allow redistribution: the records page fetches them from PubMed in your browser.

  2. Copy the screening prompt from the Start page: the criteria C1-C6 are already pasted in, with the output format (one row per record, record_id,decision,reason, decision include | exclude | unsure, a reason naming the criterion).

  3. Paste both into a new temporary chat with your AI assistant, web search off: the prompt first, the records where it says [PASTE THE RECORDS HERE].

  4. Paste the AI's answer into the scorer, as it is: no file to save. The scorer finds the table even with code fences, a sentence before or after it, or semicolons. Read the coverage line first: "Screened 20 of 60 records" is expected; fewer than 20 means the AI dropped or renamed records.

Hints
  • A prompt that starts from the criteria gets better results than "is this relevant to hand hygiene?".
  • Records without an abstract: the AI should decide on the title and mark unsure with reason no abstract. Never let it write the abstract.
  • If the answer is cut off, type continue from record [last record_id], same format.

Step 2 · Look at the errors (10 min)#

The scorer lists the missed includes (records the reference review included and the AI excluded: the costly error) and the false includes. Now you are the verifier.

  1. Open 2 of them: read the title and the abstract (the scorer links each record to PubMed).

  2. Decide yourself why the AI got them wrong. Which criterion did it use? Does the abstract say what its reason claims? Was the criterion contradicted, or just not mentioned (that is unsure, not exclude)?

  3. Check the reference too. The screening answers give the basis of every reference decision. A record that the review excluded only after reading the full text is not an error at title/abstract stage, and one record is flagged as a possible error in the reference standard.

  4. Keep one error to bring to the discussion: what the AI said, what the source says, and why.

Step 3 · Short extraction (10 min)#

One paper, Phan2020, and 5 fields of the extraction form: country, study_design, intervention_components, primary_hai_outcome, direction_of_effect.

Route 1: one tap. On the Start page tap Copy prompt + Phan2020 full text: the extraction prompt with the paper inserted, in one paste. Then go to point 3. To copy the pieces separately, use points 1 and 2.

  1. Copy the extraction prompt (Papers page or Start page): the 5 fields, their definitions and study_id = Phan2020 are already filled in.

  2. Copy the full text of Phan2020.txt (Copy and Download buttons on the Papers page) and paste it into a new temporary chat (web search off) after the prompt.

  3. Every value must come with a verbatim quote and its location (section or table), or not reported.

  4. Verify 2 quotes yourself: Ctrl+F in the paper. Is the quote there, word for word? Does it support the value?
  5. Compare with the reference values (extraction answers, after this step), or paste the answer into the scorer (tab "Short extraction"). Read the notes: some papers contradict themselves.

Ready to paste: the extraction prompt with the 5 fields (country, study_design, intervention_components, primary_hai_outcome, direction_of_effect) and study_id = Phan2020 already filled in. In a new temporary chat with web search off, paste it, then paste the paper where it says [PASTE THE TEXT OF THE PAPER, OR SAY "attached"].

Open the paper (Phan2020)
Show the prompt
You are extracting data for a systematic review. Use ONLY the paper I give you. Do not search the web or use outside knowledge.

EXTRACTION FORM (fill every field, do not add or change fields):
- country: Country where the study was conducted. Take it from Methods/Results; if the paper gives it only in the affiliation of the study hospital, report it with 'author affiliations' as location. Do not infer it from city or campaign names alone; if it is not stated anywhere, write not reported. Allowed values: free text.
- study_design: Design of the evaluation, as you would classify it (not only the authors' label). Allowed values: interrupted time series | controlled before-after | uncontrolled before-after | randomised trial | other.
- intervention_components: Components of the hand hygiene intervention. Allowed values: list, separated by ';': education/training; alcohol-based hand rub at point of care; reminders/posters; audit and feedback; leadership/institutional safety climate; patient participation; other (specify).
- primary_hai_outcome: The main clinical healthcare-associated infection outcome reported (name it as the authors do). Allowed values: free text.
- direction_of_effect: Direction of the effect on the primary HAI outcome. Allowed values: favourable | no clear effect | mixed | unfavourable.

RULES
- For every field give: value, a verbatim quote copied exactly from the paper, and the location (section, table, page).
- If the paper does not report the field, write: not reported. Do not guess.
- Do not round or convert. If there are several values (several wards, arms or time periods), list each on its own row and say which is which.

OUTPUT: only a CSV block with the header
study_id,field,value,source_quote,location
Use study_id = Phan2020.

PAPER:
[PASTE THE TEXT OF THE PAPER, OR SAY "attached"]
Hints
  • Numbers live in tables, and tables are the hardest part to parse: check table values first.
  • "Not reported" is a valid answer. A value with no quote is not a value.
  • Retrieval tools (project knowledge, notebooks) answer from fragments: if a fragment is not retrieved, the AI says "not reported" instead of "I did not see it". For one paper, give the whole text.

Discussion (last 10 minutes of the session)#

In the live session: each person brings one error they found (in step 2 or step 3) and how they caught it; the room collects them. On your own: answer each theme in writing, one or two sentences.

Theme Questions
Performance How many includes did the AI miss? Would you accept that sensitivity in a real review? Was the time saved worth the time spent checking?
Transparency Could you trace every decision and value to a sentence in the source? Which quotes were not in the paper?
Bias Which kinds of records or fields did the AI get wrong systematically (single units, bundles, values only in tables or figures, countries it inferred)?
Human oversight Where did you catch an error the AI presented with confidence? Would you sign this table?
Reproducibility Would the same prompt give the same answer twice? And how reproducible are human reviewers: would two of them, or the same one a month later, agree? What would you report so that someone else can repeat what you did?
The reference Is the reference standard always right? What did you find when the AI and the review disagreed?

Going further#

Not needed for the 30 minutes. Do these at home, or if you finish early.

  • A second run. Paste the same prompt and the same batch in a new chat and paste both answers into the scorer (Going further box): it reports how many decisions changed and Cohen's kappa. A result you cannot reproduce is not a method.

  • Research idea from Berlin: compare the reproducibility of human reviewers and AI on the same extraction task.

  • The 11 core fields. The longer extraction, with the 11 core fields of the form: the prompt is on the Papers page. Try the second paper, Mestre2012 (the paper of the demo), with the same prompt.

  • Log the discrepancies in the discrepancy log (what the AI said, what the reference says, who is right after checking the source, the error type) and fill the AI use record (tool, model, version, date, prompts): both have templates to copy or download.

  • The agent track with skills. With Claude Code or another coding agent: screen all 60 records and extract the 3 papers, with the skills of ../skills/README.md (title-abstract-screening runs two independent passes and lists the disagreements). The third paper, Al Kuwaiti 2017, is CC BY-NC: download it to your computer with python3 activity/tools/fetch_fulltext.py. Score with Python (standard library only):

    Terminal
    python3 activity/tools/score_screening.py screening_run1.csv --compare screening_run2.csv --expect-all
python3 activity/tools/score_extraction.py extraction.csv

    Chat track with Python: the same commands without --expect-all, and --fields country,study_design,intervention_components,primary_hai_outcome,direction_of_effect for the short extraction.

  • The title/abstract-stage view and the other indicators of the scorer (specificity, precision, WSS): see below.

How to read the screening score

Coverage rule (the same in the Python and the browser scorer): the metrics are computed on the records present in your answer, and the report always says how many were screened ("Screened N of 60 records"), lists the records not screened, highlights any reference include among them, and gives the sensitivity counting not-screened includes as missed. In the chat track you screen 20 records, so 40 "not screened" is expected. With --expect-all (agent track) records not screened count as exclude in every metric. unsure counts as include.

The reference is the review's final decision. Some records were excluded by the review only after reading the full text: including them at title/abstract stage is not an error. The scorer shows a "title/abstract-stage view" for this, and the gold_basis column explains each reference decision. Sensitivity (missed includes) matters most. One record is marked as a possible error in the reference standard: discuss it.

Doing it on your own (self-paced)#

Everything you need is on the website and in this repository; no facilitator, slides or group are required. Allow 60 to 90 minutes: the same three steps as the live session, with more time to verify before you look at the answers.

Block Live session On your own What to do
Get ready demo video 10 min Watch the demo video (2 min); read the key message and the criteria on this page; pick a route; turn off web search and use a temporary chat (three rules). New to AI? Follow the beginners walkthrough (chat track, for learning only)
Step 1 · Screening 10 min 15-20 min Batch 1 (R001-R020); paste the AI's answer into the scorer
Step 2 · Look at the errors 10 min 15-20 min Open the missed and false includes; decide why the AI got them wrong
Step 3 · Short extraction 10 min 15-20 min Phan2020, 5 fields, a quote for every value; verify the quotes before opening the extraction answers
Discussion 10 min 10 min Write one or two sentences per theme
Going further as you like Second run, 11 fields, discrepancy log, AI use record, agent track

You drive, then you verify. Do not let the two jobs blur: first run the AI and keep its answer as it is; then stop and become the verifier, which is the part this exercise is about. The verifier checklist:

  • Screening. As many rows came back as you sent (the scorer's coverage line); no record_id missing, repeated or renamed.
  • At least 2 decisions (one of them an exclude) checked against the abstract: does the abstract say what the reason claims?
  • Every exclude names a criterion that the abstract clearly contradicts, not one it merely does not mention (that is unsure).
  • No reason uses a rule that is not in C1-C6 (country, "low quality", date...).
  • Extraction. At least 2 quotes found with Ctrl+F in the paper, character for character; every number in a value appears in its quote.
  • Every not reported searched in the paper with synonyms (infection rate, nosocomial, hospital-acquired, per 1000 patient-days).

When to open the answers. Screening answers after step 1, extraction answers after step 3. The scorer shows the screening reference as soon as you score, so screen first. The reference review itself and the facilitator guide name the included studies: open them only after the exercise. If you use an agent, do not let it read answers/ before then either.

Reading the score without a facilitator.

  1. Coverage line first. "Screened 20 of 60 records (40 not screened)" is expected for batch 1. Fewer than 20 screened means the AI dropped or renamed records: that is already a finding.

  2. Missed includes. The costly error at this stage. For each one, open the abstract: which criterion did the AI use, and was it right to?

  3. False includes. Look at the gold_basis: a record excluded by the review only after reading the full text is not an error at title/abstract stage.

  4. Extraction. A quote that is not in the paper, a value where the paper reports nothing (unsupported) and a not reported for something the paper does report (false absent) matter more than small wording differences; read the notes of the reference values, because some papers contradict themselves.

  5. The reference can be wrong. One record is flagged as a possible error in the reference standard. Check the source before deciding who is right.

After scoring, the sections "What to expect in screening", "What to expect in extraction" and "Interpreting the scores" of the facilitator guide are your debrief.

Discuss with yourself. Answer the questions of the discussion in writing. Then the one that matters most: would you sign this screening and this table as they came out of the AI, and what would you need to check first?

What next.

  • Do more: everything under Going further.

  • Read the five starting references, especially the position statement of Cochrane, the Campbell Collaboration, JBI and CEE and the RAISE recommendations, which say how AI use should be overseen and reported.

  • Use the prompt library for the other review stages, or the agent skills if you already work with coding agents.

  • Before using AI in a real review, be honest about your AI literacy and skills (see the warning above), and pilot any tool on a sample with known answers, as you just did.

  • Tell us what broke or what surprised you: open an issue.

If the website (records page, scorer) is not available


The records page and the scorer are on GitHub Pages. If they do not open, everything still works:

  • Records, with Python 3 and internet access to PubMed: Option B of the beginners walkthrough: python3 activity/tools/fetch_abstracts.py, then python3 beginners/make_batches.py activity/data/local/screening_records_full.csv --size 20, and paste beginners/batches/screening_batch_01.md (R001-R020). Both files are local and git-ignored: do not publish them.

  • Records, without Python: open data/screening_records.csv; for each record of R001-R020 with an empty abstract, open https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/<pmid>/ and copy the abstract word for word. Never ask the AI to find or write an abstract: it may invent one.

  • Both pages on your own computer: cd docs && python3 -m http.server 8000, then open http://localhost:8000/batch.html and http://localhost:8000/scorer.html (the same pages, served locally).

  • Score with the Python scorers (standard library only): save the AI's answer as a text file and run the commands under Going further; without Python, after step 1 compare your 20 rows by hand with answers/screening_gold.csv.
